stack: React 19 + Vite + TypeScript (scaffolder substrate); Lit + HTMX (existing preview)
schema_note: references/schemas/library-candidates.schema.json is NOT installed with kbd-analyze (only SKILL.md ships). Shape follows the field set described inline in SKILL.md; unvalidated.

budget.tier4_skipped_reason: T1-T3 produced a decisive finding that reframes the phase; further breadth would not change the recommendation.

headline_finding.summary: A2UI is a real external protocol with a 16,230-star upstream (a2ui-project/a2ui, pushed 2026-08-28) and an official Apache-2.0 React renderer (@a2ui/react). Our schema is namespaced artifact-refiner.dev, cites no upstream, and diverges from the real protocol at every structural level.

data_binding.ours: top-level bindings map with literal/ref/expression kinds

document_shape.ours: { version, metadata, bindings, root } — a single tree
document_shape.upstream: envelope stream: createSurface / updateComponents / updateDataModel / deleteSurface / callFunction / actionResponse

component_vocabulary.upstream: catalog.json declaring an explicit component set

headline_finding.consequence: Specs our refiner validates are NOT A2UI-protocol documents. Any host built to our schema cannot consume real agent output, and any real A2UI agent output fails our validator. This is the TOOL_CALL_ARGS_DELTA defect class from phase-7, one level up: not a wrong enum value but a wrong document model.

correction_to_assess.claim: A2UI is a declarative component tree with no transport — 'the spec is a static document', 'arguably no store at all'
correction_to_assess.evidence: Upstream specification/v1_0/docs/a2ui_protocol.md: 'The A2UI Protocol facilitates the dynamic rendering of user interfaces by streaming JSON objects from an agent to a renderer... allowing for progressive rendering as the renderer processes incoming messages.' The glossary defines an A2UI message as supporting streaming, finished or interrupted. Transports are JSON Lines streams.
correction_to_assess.impact: F-1 argued the phase-7 substrate does not transfer BECAUSE A2UI has no stream. The opposite is true: A2UI is streaming-first, so the store/subscription/progressive-accumulation substrate transfers MORE than assess concluded, not less. The AG-UI event vocabulary still differs, but the architectural shape is the same.

gaps.title: Our A2UI schema is not the A2UI protocol
gaps.rationale: Discovered during analyze; not present in the assessment's gap report. Every other gap's framing depends on whether we align to upstream or keep a local dialect.

options.name: Align to upstream A2UI v1.0
pros: catalog system replaces our ad-hoc componentType pattern
cons: breaking change to a shipped domain (PR #1)
refiner must be reworked to the envelope model

options.name: Keep the local dialect, rename it
cons: the name A2UI is taken and means something else
future readers will assume protocol conformance

options.name: Support both
cons: two document models, two renderers, roughly double the surface

gaps.title: Renderer component types cannot match any conformant spec
gaps.note: Under alignment @a2ui/react implements the catalog vocabulary and the local componentType pattern disappears. Under the dialect this stands exactly as assessed.

gaps.title: No template injector; no HTML ever produced
gaps.note: A runtime React host renders from the spec and never substitutes {{A2UI_JSON}} into a static template. Only reading (a) needs an injector.

gaps.title: Bindings never resolved
gaps.note: Upstream uses DynamicString wrappers plus updateDataModel envelope messages, not a top-level bindings map with literal/ref/expression kinds. Aligning replaces the gap rather than fixing it.

gaps.title: Only 3 component types implemented; example needs 4+
gaps.note: @a2ui/react ships the component set; hand-implementing types is only work under the dialect.

gaps.title: Phase scope undefined: finish preview vs emit a scaffolder
gaps.note: Still open (assess Q1), but now downstream of G-8: aligning makes the scaffolder reading substantially cheaper because the renderer is adopted rather than written.

gaps.title: expression binding evaluation strategy undecided
gaps.note: The protocol defines callFunction with callableFrom metadata instead of arbitrary expression strings, so the security question dissolves under alignment. Live under the dialect — recommend rejecting expression in v1.

gaps.title: Preview loads Lit/HTMX/Alpine from unpkg @latest
gaps.note: Five unpinned CDN loads (assess F-6). Independent of G-8; relevant because a browser-DOM verification against @latest dependencies is a flaky test.

candidates.name: @a2ui/react
candidates.rationale: The official renderer for the real protocol. If G-8 resolves toward alignment, this eliminates G-1, G-4, and most of G-2 outright — there is no reason to hand-write a component interpreter that upstream already ships and maintains.
risks: Publish cadence lags the repo: repo pushed 2026-08-28, package last published 2026-07-17 (~6 weeks). The npm artifact is not tracking main closely.
`@a2ui/markdown-it` is declared as `*` — an unbounded version range in a published dependency, which is a packaging smell and a supply-chain risk.
peerDependency react ^19.2.7 — VERIFIED satisfied (npm latest 19.2.8; scaffold-react-vite.sh:148 targets React 19). No longer an open risk.
candidates.peer_compat_verified: react ^19.2.7 vs npm latest 19.2.8 — satisfied; scaffold-react-vite.sh:148 targets React 19

candidates.name: Existing Lit renderer in a2ui-preview-template.html
candidates.rationale: Handles three lowercase component types that cannot match our own schema's PascalCase pattern (assess F-2), resolves no bindings (assess F-4), and implements neither our dialect nor upstream A2UI. Whatever G-8 decides, this is not a foundation — it is roughly 30 lines of switch statement that has never rendered a conformant spec.
candidates.salvageable: The surrounding preview shell (brand CSS variables, header/main layout, screenshot harness) is reusable independent of the renderer.

candidates.name: @easyops-cn/a2ui-sdk
candidates.rationale: Not published to npm despite a Context7 entry. Unavailable as a dependency.

candidates.name: CopilotKit/generative-ui
candidates.rationale: Umbrella library spanning AG-UI, A2UI, and Open-JSON-UI. Same verdict as phase-7's @copilotkit/react-core: a full framework whose opinions collide with this repo's scaffolder conventions. Revisit only if the goal expands to a complete agentic-UI product surface.

candidates.name: @a2ui/web_core
candidates.rationale: Framework-agnostic engine beneath @a2ui/react — deps are zod, date-fns, zod-to-json-schema, @preact/signals-core, with NO React peer. Arrives transitively for a React host. Publishes more recently than @a2ui/react (2026-08-03 vs 2026-07-17), so the staleness concern is specific to the React wrapper, not the stack. Named so plan knows the non-React seam exists.

candidates.name: A2UI.Blazor / a2ui-swift / A2UI-Android / a2ui-react-native
candidates.rationale: Ports to .NET, Swift, Android, and React Native — none consumable from a Vite/React TypeScript host. Corroborative value only: four independent ports across four ecosystems is evidence A2UI is a real multi-implementation standard, which is what makes our divergence consequential.

open_questions_resolved.question: Q2 (from assess): Lit + HTMX or React?
open_questions_resolved.answer: React, UNCONDITIONALLY. Under alignment, @a2ui/react is the official renderer. Under the dialect, still React — the scaffolder substrate is React (phase-7's wrapper, architectural ESLint, store/hook/component layering), and the existing Lit renderer has never rendered a conformant spec, so 'keep Lit' means REWRITE in Lit, not reuse. What G-8 changes is whether the renderer is adopted or written, not the framework.

open_questions_remaining: G-8 (NEW, blocking): align our A2UI to the real protocol, rename the local dialect, or support both? Not an analyze decision — it changes the meaning of a shipped domain and invalidates published examples.

Q1 (from assess, still open): finish the preview pipeline, or emit a scaffolder? Now subordinate to G-8 — aligning upstream makes the scaffolder reading substantially cheaper, since @a2ui/react does the rendering.
Q3 (from assess): expression-binding evaluation. Moot if aligning upstream (the protocol defines callFunction with callableFrom metadata instead); live if keeping the dialect.

upstream_provenance.note: specification/v1_0/** paths are upstream GitHub files, NOT in this repo. Cited as external protocol authority; re-verify via Context7 or by fetching upstream.
upstream_provenance.locally_verifiable: our schema $id is artifact-refiner.dev; grep over references/domain/a2ui.md finds no external spec reference
